modern: To look for a fig in winter is a madman’s act: such is the man who looks for his child when it is no longer allowed.
original: To look for the fig in winter is a mad-man’s act: such is he who looks for his child when it is no longer allowed.

notification_original: To look for the fig in winter is a mad-man’s act: such is he who looks for his child when it is no longer allowed.

explained.summary: Taken from Epictetus: looking for figs in winter is madness, and so is longing for a child once nature no longer allows you to have them. This is one of the hardest Stoic ideas, and Marcus, who lost several children, doesn’t soften it. Everything comes in its season, and demanding what nature has taken away only adds to the suffering.
